mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for three consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand and corporate earnings pressure, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 4.5% and remains above for 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of sustained UNRATE > 4.5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 2-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) exceeding 2% signals weakening household demand, which reduces earnings growth and compresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of RSAFS decline > 2% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month acceleration in industrial production (INDPRO) above 0.5% signals improving manufacturing activity and earnings momentum, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of INDPRO acceleration > 0.5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and a fall in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 1% over two months signals a deepening labor market downturn, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls by > 1% over 2 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of simultaneous UNRATE rise and PAYEMS fall > 1% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the federal funds rate above 5% signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises above 5% and remains there for 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of FEDFUNDS > 5% for 3 months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) below 1,200 thousand units signals weakening residential investment and consumer confidence, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls below 1,200 and remains there for 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of HOUST < 1,200 for 3 months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) exceeding 2% signals weakening household demand, which reduces earnings growth and compresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of RSAFS decline > 2% (t-test p > 0.05).
